sources.title: KGHM, South32 kick off $725M Sierra Gorda expansion
evidence: KGHM and South32 (ASX, LSE, JSE: S32) have officially begun a $725 million expansion of their Sierra Gorda mine in Chile, expected to lift annual copper output to nearly 200,000 tonnes.

The fourth grinding line will increase the Antofagasta operation's ore-processing capacity by 26%. Construction is scheduled to begin in January 2027, with the expanded plant expected to reach full capacity in the second half of 2030.

sources.title: India targets 600 million tons steel capacity by 2047, secretary says
evidence: India's new steel policy plans 600 million metric tons of steelmaking capacity by 2047 and is a roadmap for the next two decades, the country's steel secretary said on Tuesday, adding that it will be released to the public domain soon.
India's steelmaking capacity stood at 220 million tons as of fiscal 2026.
The steel ministry expects iron ore demand at 772 million tons and plans to secure access to high-grade reserves by pursuing foreign assets and joint ventures, the document said.

The ministry also expects coking coal demand to reach 214 million tons, the document said, with the government planning to diversify its sourcing via "strategic global outreach" and acquire overseas assets.

sources.title: Thailand's PTTGC, SCGC expect to finalize JV details by Oct 2026
evidence: SINGAPORE (ICIS)–Thailand's PTT Global Chemical (PTTGC) and SCG Chemicals (SCGC) are advancing talks for a proposed joint venture (JV) to combine their olefins and polyolefins businesses, the companies said in separate statements.
PTTGC and SCGC will then be submitting an application to the Trade Competition Commission of Thailand (TCCT) for approval.

SCGC, meanwhile, is expected to contribute its Thai crackers, PE and polypropylene (PP) plants, along with investments in its subsidiaries Siam Polyethylene, Siam Synthetic Latex, Thai MMA and Bangkok Synthetics.

sources.title: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports, one cancels cargoes, sources say
evidence: SINGAPORE, Oct 1 (Reuters) - Chinese refiners have suspended exports of oil products to ‌regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice from ‌Beijing, four people briefed on the matter said on Thursday.

As China looks to safeguard domestic ​supplies, state oil major PetroChina cancelled on Wednesday a handful of its gasoline and jet fuel shipments that were planned for October, three of the sources said.

It is not ​clear if Beijing would resume ​permitting refiners' exports after the holiday ends on October ‌7, the sources said, adding that ​it could depend ​on domestic fuel inventories and refining output.
